subject: sociology
title: Theory & Methods: Modernity vs Postmodernity
welcome_lead: Industrial certainty gives way to liquid uncertainty.
meta_desc: A-Level Sociology theory modernity postmodernity Lyotard Bauman.
final_note: Postmodernists doubt the big stories; theorists of late modernity revise them.

concepts.def: C18-C20 era of industry, science, nation-state, big narratives.
Late C20+ — fragmented, media-saturated, sceptical of grand theory.
Baudrillard — simulation more real than reality.

walkthroughs.body_html: Modernity emerged with industrial revolution: nation states, capitalism, secularisation, science. Classical sociology (Marx, Weber, Durkheim) was its self-description. Big optimistic stories of progress dominated.

Lyotard (1979): postmodern is 'incredulity towards metanarratives'. Baudrillard (1981): media creates hyperreality — Disneyland, Gulf War as TV event. Bauman (2000): liquid modernity — fluid identities, broken communities, no anchor.

Giddens (1990) rejects 'postmodernity' — we are in late modernity. Increased reflexivity: we monitor and reshape our lives. Beck (1992): risk society — modern risks (climate, nuclear) are manufactured by modernity itself. The fight over the label continues.

mcqs.q: Lyotard defined postmodernity as 'incredulity' towards what?
Bauman's term for fluid identity in late modernity is what?

numericals.q: In what year did Lyotard publish 'The Postmodern Condition'?

free_texts.q: Who coined the term 'risk society' in 1992?
